title: The Thistle That Learned to Multiply
story: Pucklemire the Splitting Thistle grows in the goat meadow, and every swing of a blade makes each thistle burst into four. The goatherds have chopped and chopped and now cannot find their goats. Mr 6 stops, sheathes his sword, and does the far scarier thing: arithmetic.
question: There is 1 thistle. Each chop turns every thistle into 4 thistles. After 4 chops, how many thistles more than 100 are there?
hint: Multiply by 4 once for each chop — 1, 4, 16, and so on — then remember the question asks how many MORE than 100.
victory: Mr 6 announced "one hundred fifty-six more than a hundred, and that's why I'm not chopping," and Pucklemire — starved of blades — folded back into a single grumpy purple weed. The goats ate it.
imagePrompt: A bristling purple thistle-monster mid-split into four copies in a misty green goat meadow, with a small numeral 6 knight holding up a firm 'stop' hand instead of a sword.
solution: Multiply by 4 for each chop: 1 → 4 → 16 → 64 → 256 after 4 chops.
The question asks how many MORE than 100: 256 − 100 = 156.
praise: Doubling-style growth by repeated multiplying was the right idea — the final subtraction of 100 was the step still waiting.
